 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the respondent/driver cum owner of the offending vehicle in O.P.(MV) No.258/2019 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, North Paravur (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 25/02/2020.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, North Paravur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent herein is the claim petitioner.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, 09/03/2019 at about 11:30 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-42/D-6430 through Paravur-Varapuzha road from south to north, car bearing registration no.KL-46/2433 driven by the respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The respondent filed written statement contending that 2025:KER:66932 the petition is false and baseless.
The averments in the petition regarding nature of injuries sustained and the negligence attributed against the respondent were denied.
The compensation claimed under various heads was contended to be exorbitant.
4. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A5 series
were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Exts.B1 and B2 were marked on the side of the respondent.

5. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 97,300/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the respondent/driver cum owner has come up in appeal.
6. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
Though notice was served on the respondent herein, that is, the claim petitioner, he neither appeared in person nor through counsel.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.

2 8.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent/driver cum owner that he was not given opportunity to disprove the case of negligence put forward by the claimant.

He had filed I.A.No.5/2020 to summon the SHO, who had conducted investigation and had submitted Ext.A3 charge sheet alleging the commission of offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 IPC;
Section 146 read with Section 196 of the Act.
However, the application was not allowed by the Tribunal causing serious prejudice to him, as he was unable to establish his defence that he was not negligent in driving the vehicle.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the respondent/driver cum owner seeks a remand of the matter so that he may get an opportunity to prove his contentions in the written statement.
9. As noticed earlier though notice has been served on the claim petitioner he has chosen not to appear either in person or 2025:KER:66932 through counsel.
I.A.No.5 of 2020 was not allowed by the Tribunal, the order reads thus- "No sufficient ground shown to issue summons to the witness.
Hence petition closed."
Therefore, it is apparent that an opportunity was not granted to the respondent-driver to establish his defence causing prejudice and injustice to him.

Hence in the facts and circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice, I am constrained to remand the matter to the Tribunal for giving an opportunity to the respondent/driver cum owner to establish his case as contended in the written statement.

As the accident is of the year 2019, the Tribunal shall endeavour to dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible at any rate within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.

Sd/-
